grammar_systems.name: Grammar Systems: Rules Generate Structure
grammar_systems.truth: A handful of rules, iterated, becomes a forest. Grammars are the DNA of procedural generation.
grammar_systems.qfep_connection: Grammars are pure F (deterministic rules) that generate E(S) (structural variety). Stochastic grammars add controlled entropy. L-systems are morphogenesis made computational.
grammar_systems.description: Formal grammars as generative systems. Markov chains predict from history, N-grams capture local patterns, L-systems grow plants and cities. Context-free, context-sensitive, stochasticâ€”different rule types for different generations.
learning_objectives: Formal grammars: rules that rewrite symbols

artifact_groups.rationale: Markov chains as generative grammar: transition probabilities predict next states from history. Clipboard logs the chain, tree variant shows branching probability paths.
N-grams as local context windows: same Markov chain artifact reconfigured for N-gram analysis. Character and word-level pattern capture — the statistical foundation of language models.
Voxel grammar synthesis: city generator and context-sensitive tree from L-systems, 3D cellular automata tree, voxel noise and ROI volumes. Five artifacts showing grammars building worlds from rules.
